page: Google Cloud Platform ct5p-hightpu-2t is a hardware-accelerated instance within the TPU Machines family designed for high-throughput machine learning workloads. The host system is provisioned with 104 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs and 224 GB of system RAM, maintaining a compute-biased ratio of approximately 2.15 GB of system memory per vCPU. Compute resources operate on dedicated physical cores to prevent neighbor contention during intense preprocessing cycles.

At the core of the configuration are two Google TPU v5p processors delivering an aggregate of 190 GB of high-bandwidth VRAM. The system features no bundled local storage disks, requiring external cloud block storage for operating system images, dataset ingestion, and model checkpointing. Network provisioning does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which reflects an architecture intended to operate within private cloud networks or behind dedicated gateways.

Resource efficiency on this machine type centers on offloading intensive matrix operations directly to the TPU processors. While the 104 host vCPUs adequately drive data preprocessing and pipeline coordination, general scalar computation is secondary to accelerator throughput. This balance makes the instance appropriate for distributed training runs, transformer model fine-tuning, natural language processing, and scalable tensor-based scientific simulations.
description: Google Cloud Platform ct5p-hightpu-2t is an accelerator-focused instance belonging to the TPU Machines family, engineered for deep learning training and inference pipelines. The instance couples 104 dedicated x86_64 host vCPUs with 224 GB of system memory, yielding roughly 2.15 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by two Google TPU v5p processors containing a combined total of 190 GB of high-bandwidth VRAM. The system contains no bundled local storage disks, necessitating external network-attached volumes for data persistence and dataset staging. Furthermore, complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included with the standard allocation. In terms of resource allocation, the high accelerator density relative to host compute optimizes hardware utilization for matrix-heavy tensor operations rather than general scalar computing. The ct5p-hightpu-2t instance is primarily suited for large language model pre-training, fine-tuning, computer vision model training, and distributed scientific tensor computation.
